label: Rove

names.text: Taken from the Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the article gives the Occitan name "Cabra dau Rove".

about.text: A goat breed from the scrublands around Le Rove, a village near Marseille in France. It was first bred for meat, but farmers turned to dairying because the French goat-meat market was poor. Its whole milk is the base of the protected cheese Brousse du Rove.

sources.text: Rove goat article, read on WebFetch: the meat origin, the switch to dairying and the Le Rove village. Brousse du Rove article, read on WebFetch: the cheese is "based on whole goat's milk of the breed Rove" and the goats live on the scrublands of Rove, l'Étoile and other massifs around Marseille.

origin.place: Le Rove, a village near Marseille in Provence. The goats live on the scrublands of Rove, l'Étoile and other massifs around Marseille.

sources.text: Rove goat article: the name comes from Le Rove, a small village near Marseille, and the breed is "first domesticated in France". Brousse du Rove article: the scrubland massifs. Origin accounts found in search text conflict (Provençal landrace, Phoenician introduction), so they are not used. No formation dates are sourced.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "as of 2003, more than 5,000 registered Roves are on French farms." The count is a floor, and it is more than twenty years old.

Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "The goat was originally bred for meat" and farmers switched to dairying because "the French market for goat meat was poor". The article does not call it dual-purpose.

facts.v: Brousse du Rove, a fresh goat's milk cheese, received AOC (AOP) status on 31 May 2018.

sources.text: Brousse du Rove article, read on WebFetch: "On 31 May 2018, Brousse du Rove received an Appellation d'origine contrôlée." and "(AOC and AOP)". The article describes it as a fresh cheese, which the search text also says is unaged.

gaps: No milk yield per lactation or per year and no lactation length; no current risk status (the Wikipedia article says only that the breed was "previously considered endangered", with no year, and no DAD-IS record was readable); no population count after 2003; no formation dates; no composition figures. The Brousse du Rove article does not state the herd-only rule that search text mentioned, so it is not used.
